source.title: Masked Autoencoders for Microscopy are Scalable Learners of Cellular Biology
source.authors: Oren Kraus; Kian Kenyon-Dean; Saber Saberian; Maryam Fallah; Peter McLean; Jess Leung; Vasudev Sharma; Ayla Khan; Jia Balakrishnan; Safiye Celik; D. Beaini; Maciej Sypetkowski; C. Cheng; Kristen Morse; Maureen Makes; Ben Mabey; Berton A. Earnshaw

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports downstream retrieval and transfer results, including transfer to JUMP-CP with different experimental conditions and channel structure. It does not test the claim versions about same-distribution train/test error, memorization, or the listed factors and measures of the generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The JUMP-CP results concern transfer across datasets and experimental conditions, which the claim explicitly treats as separate from same-distribution generalization. The paper also reports scaling of biological-relationship recall and comparisons between WSL and MAE models, not train/test error gaps.
record.test_reason: The study measures microscopy representation quality, biological relationship recall, and transfer across experimental settings. It does not test any specified version. Model-size comparisons do not establish interpolation thresholds; convolutional versus transformer comparisons do not compare convolutional with fully connected classifiers. Larger batches and Lion are reported to improve downstream performance jointly, without a fixed-epoch batch-size comparison or an adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that microscopy MAE performance scales with model and training-set size and that channel-agnostic MAEs transfer across channel configurations. They also conclude that their Fourier-domain reconstruction loss stabilizes large-model training. Transfer benefits are task-dependent: sibling retrieval remains below CellProfiler.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains self-supervised masked autoencoders on microscopy data and evaluates biological relationship retrieval, feature prediction, and cross-dataset transfer; it does not investigate the claim's natural-label generalization gap.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that batch correction changes biological-relationship recall; JUMP-CP performance varies by retrieval task and model.

fits_no_version.finding: On JUMP-CP, CA-MAE achieves perturbation retrieval of .95 ± .05 versus CellProfiler's .53 ± .30, but sibling retrieval of .02 ± .02 versus .13 ± .07.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Channel-agnostic microscopy representations transfer across channel configurations, with benefits depending on the retrieval task.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 compares ImageNet-pretrained, weakly supervised, masked-autoencoder, and CellProfiler representations on two microscopy retrieval tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining method and representation choice affect cross-dataset microscopy retrieval performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 4.2 and A.2.3 report improved training dynamics and downstream performance using larger batches together with Lion rather than the recommended batch size and AdamW settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jointly changing batch size and optimizer can improve microscopy MAE training and downstream representation quality.

record.problems: The JUMP-CP results are averaged over cell types, modalities, and time-points in Table 4; the study states that direct comparison with the external HCS platform is impossible because assay technology, cell lines, and modeling methodology differ.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under matched architectures and training recipes.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers trained from scratch, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under controlled tuning, including training and held-out performance.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe adaptations remove them.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the specific variables and comparisons required by V1–V8, rather than a blanket exclusion of transfer results. Table 4 uncertainties are standard deviations across cell types, perturbation modalities, and time points. No additional result testing a specified version was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and same-distribution generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and their same-distribution test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the effect of local connectivity on test error.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and their same-distribution held-out performance under controlled tuning.
The effect of batch size on the train/test generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on held-out error and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train/test error gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
